item.title: Beijing Signals Business as Usual After Midterms
item.description: Beijing offered a guarded official reaction to the Republican midterm loss, even as celebratory hashtags trended widely across Chinese social media. Bloomberg's Stephen Engle says the shift could introduce fresh uncertainty into US-China relations, especially around Taiwan and pending arms sales. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: DSA’s Raman Beats Bass in Los Angeles Mayor Race, DDHQ Projects
item.description: Nithya Raman is projected to win the Los Angeles mayor’s race, according to Decision Desk HQ, ousting incumbent Karen Bass and putting a democratic socialist in charge of the second-largest US city.
item.dc:creator: John Gittelsohn

item.title: Ted Cruz Laments GOP’s Midterm Losses and Texas Turning Blue
item.description: Texas Senator Ted Cruz called the sweeping Democratic victories across the US a “blue tsunami” and delivered a scathing assessment of his party’s historic losses, including in his home state, where Republicans were ousted from nearly every major office.
item.dc:creator: Cameron Fozi

item.title: Leon Black Sues Congressman Garcia Over Epstein Statements
item.description: Apollo Global Management co-founder Leon Black sued a Congressman from California for allegedly making false statements about the billionaire’s relationship with sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
item.dc:creator: Bob Van Voris

item.title: Kalshi Head of Research on Midterms Accuracy
item.description: Nicole Kagan, Head of Research at Kalshi, joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss the prediction platform's accuracy on 2026 midterm election night, saying that bets on the platform were over 98% accurate across Tuesday's races. She points out that traders rapidly repriced races like the South Carolina senate race within minutes of polls closing, and often before news outlets called results. Kagan also discusses how her team digests the outcomes of trades on major events, and how participants gather information to support their bets. She also discusses how institutional investors might apply the platform's probability and price discovery component in their daily work. Kagan speaks with Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Democratic Sweep Redraws Political Map
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Leon Panetta, former Secretary of Defense and White House Chief of Staff, says whether Susie Wiles remains White House Chief of Staff depends on her relationship with President Donald Trump, a relationship Panetta says appears to be good. Kendall Scudder, Texas Democratic Party Chair, says Democrats' statewide wins in Texas were the result of people working hard over multiple election cycles and rebuilding the party's infrastructure. Scudder says Elon Musk got a tough message that "Texas is not for sale." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Claude Lowers ChatGPT’s Lead in $1.4 Billion UK Consumer AI Market
item.description: UK consumers are spending over £1 billion ($1.4 billion) a year on artificial intelligence subscriptions, with Anthropic eating into OpenAI’s lead, research showed on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Reid and Tom Rees

item.title: Trump Talks Ballroom & Arch After Election Loss
item.description: Bloomberg's Jeff Mason joined the show to discuss the White House reaction to Republican midterm losses, President Trump's focus on the ballroom and Trump's acknowledgment that higher gasoline prices tied to the Iran war contributed to the defeat. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s Special Edition of "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Scudder Says Texas Is Not for Sale
item.description: Kendall Scudder, Texas Democratic Party Chair, says Democrats' statewide wins in Texas were the result of people working hard over multiple election cycles and rebuilding the party's infrastructure. Scudder says Elon Musk got a tough message that "Texas is not for sale." Scudder says Texas is open for business, but communities should have a say in data center development instead of finding out after decisions have already been made. Scudder believes Democrats' priorities should include corruption reform, reducing property taxes and rolling back school vouchers while strengthening public schools. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s Special Edition of "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Panetta Says Voters Sent Trump a Message on Iran War
item.description: Leon Panetta, former Secretary of Defense and White House Chief of Staff, says whether Susie Wiles remains White House Chief of Staff depends on her relationship with President Donald Trump, a relationship Panetta says appears to be good. Panetta says Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has little credibility with either Democrats or Republicans on Capitol Hill, has failed to keep Congress adequately informed and says Trump will eventually have to decide whether to keep him in the job. Panetta says Trump has to recognize that the American people have spoken clearly and do not support the war with Iran. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s Special Edition of "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Businessweek Daily: Dems Stage Midterm Sweep (Podcast)
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
Riding a tide of voter angst, Democrats swept into power in Congress, with outrage over the cost of living and the war in Iran leading to a thundering rebuke of President Donald Trump and his party just two years after his dominant White House comeback. In a seismic political shift, Democrats’ strength suggested a breakdown of the coalition that delivered Trump a second term. The election results threaten to slow the pace of the AI infrastructure buildout, with policymakers potentially turning up the heat on increasingly unpopular data center projects.
On today's episode:
Joe Mathieu, Bloomberg 'Balance of Power' Co-Host Brody Ford, Bloomberg News Tech Reporter Nathan Dean, Bloomberg Intelligence Senior US Policy Analyst Joe Lovinger, Bloomberg News Texas Reporter (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Democratic Sweep, Markets Rally & AI Stocks Slide
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Morgan Stanley Wealth Management Executive Director, Head of Policy & Geopolitical Strategy Monica Guerra, American Action Forum President Douglas Holtz-Eakin, Baird Senior Equity Research Analyst Michael Ha, JC2 Ventures Founder & CEO John Chambers, Scotts Miracle-Gro President & CEO Nate Baxter, Cantor Fitzgerald Asset Management Chief Market Strategist Eric Johnston, CFRA Research Senior VP & Equity Analyst Angelo Zino, 248 Ventures Chief Investment Strategist Lindsey Bell, Future Standard CEO Edwin Conway, & Host Hotels & Resorts CEO & President Jim Risoleo. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Edward Jones’ Andy Blocker on US Midterm Elections
item.description: Andy Blocker, Head of Policy, Regulatory and Government Relations at Edward Jones, said research shows nearly 85% of Americans are experiencing some form of financial stress. Drawing on about 100,000 client conversations a day across all 3,144 counties, he said concerns are similar across red and blue areas: whether people have enough money to cover current bills and save for retirement. He speaks with Vonnie Quinn on "The Close" on November 3, 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Only One Town Out of Dozens in US Voted in Favor of Data Centers
item.description: Voters in dozens of towns across the US sent a clear message against data centers in Tuesday’s elections — with one notable exception.
item.dc:creator: Miquéla V Thornton and Brody Ford

item.title: Economic Frustrations Flip GOP Strongholds Blue
item.description: Democrats scored sweeping victories in the midterm elections, taking control of both chambers of Congress and making unexpected gains in traditionally Republican territory. Schwab political analyst and host of the WashintgonWise Podcast Michael Townsend says the results reflect voter frustration over affordability and put pressure on Democrats to move quickly from campaigning against President Trump to delivering on their economic promises. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Republican Blame Game Starts as 2028 Hopefuls Angle for Position
item.description: The Republican Party’s generational collapse in this week’s midterm elections ushered in a wave of finger-pointing largely aimed at the Oval Office, exposing deep fissures within the party and opening the door for 2028 hopefuls to hone their message.
item.dc:creator: Josh Wingrove and Jeff Mason

item.title: US and Allies Talk Ukraine Recovery Ahead of Russia Meeting
item.description: Ukraine and its European allies discussed the country’s economic recovery and funding requirements for its war effort during talks with US officials, hours after President Donald Trump’s Republican Party suffered a drubbing in the midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Palasciano and Daryna Krasnolutska

item.title: Canada, China Extend Tariff Deal, Aim to Boost Canadian Exports
item.description: Canada and China extended a deal to lower Beijing’s agricultural tariffs through the end of 2028, while pledging to continue discussions on boosting Canadian exports to the Asian superpower.
item.dc:creator: Laura Dhillon Kane

item.title: Supreme Court President Flees Bolivia Citing Threats
item.description: Bolivia’s Supreme Court President Romer Saucedo said he fled abroad after receiving threats, while prosecutors say he faces at least two criminal investigations and are seeking an international alert for his capture.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Mendoza

item.title: China Keeps Faith in Trump as ‘Total Defeat’ Adds New Risks
item.description: As Chinese netizens pored over the wreckage of the Republican losses in the midterm US elections, the hashtag “Trump Total Defeat” went viral on microblogging platform Weibo, garnering more than 70 million views by Wednesday evening.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News
